# kurasu: architecture rules

verified: 2026-10-19

Answers how kurasu's backend code is split and which rules its Effect code follows.

## Knowledge

- `packages/core` defines services named after a job (sessions, polls, access, mailer) and their ports. It imports no adapter and nothing from Cloudflare, Alchemy, Drizzle or jose.
- Adapters live outside core: the D1 adapters in `packages/database`, the R2, Email Sending, JWT and Durable Object adapters in `apps/api`. The apps wire the core services to their adapters; packages never import apps.
- Expected failures are typed errors declared with Schema; the code does not catch defects as if they were expected.
- Decode everything that enters at a boundary (a request body, a stored row, a message) with its schema before using it.
- The Worker reads configuration with Effect `Config` where it is built and passes it to the layers as plain values (`Access.layer(webOrigin)`, `JoseSessionTokens(jwtSecret)`). Secrets come from varlock: `.env.schema` declares them and `.env.local`, out of git, holds them. The mail binding and the D1 resource also read two test-only variables, `KURASU_MAIL_ALLOWED_DESTINATIONS` and `KURASU_D1_IMPORT_FILES`, which `.env.schema` declares without a default, so `Config.option` reads them as absent outside the API tests.
- Declare Alchemy resources outside the Worker's runtime path, because a Worker's initialization runs once at deploy and again when the isolate starts. The API Worker builds its HTTP app, with every layer that reads D1, inside `fetch`, because the bindings exist only when the isolate starts (see `alchemy/local-dev`).
- Reads are bounded (a list has a maximum) and paginate by key, not by offset.
- D1 has no transactions: writes that must land together go in one batch.

## Sources

- `.scratch/aula-virtual/program-design/kurasu.md`, branches 1 to 4 and Standards.
- `app/apps/api/src/worker.ts`.
# kurasu: API shape

verified: 2026-10-19

Answers how kurasu's HTTP API is laid out: what is a route, what is a filter, and what travels inside a resource.

## Knowledge

- Each resource has one endpoint, never nested: `/api/<resource>` and `/api/<resource>/{id}`. The one exception is a resource's binary content, at `/{id}/file` (`GET /api/materials/{id}/file`).
- The student uses `/api/<resource>` and the teacher `/api/admin/<resource>`; each side gets only the operations it needs.
- The id of another resource goes in as a filter (`?sessionId=`) or in the body, never in the path.
- A resource includes the values that belong to it: the student's vote is a field of the poll (`myResponse`) and of the question (`myVote`), set with a `PATCH` on that resource.
- A list returns a summary and the detail returns the full resource (`SessionSummary` and `Session`).
- Actions that are not resources, such as requesting a login link or opening a session, stay as actions under `/api/auth/`.
- A malformed teacher request answers a typed 400 and stores nothing: `InvalidPollContent` for poll content of another type (options outside `choice`, scale labels outside `scale`) and `InvalidUpload` for a multipart upload whose fields come after the file or do not decode. Changing the access of a user id that does not exist answers `UserNotFound` (404).
- Every endpoint behind the login also answers the access middleware's errors (requesting a link and opening a session have no middleware): `Unauthenticated`, `NoAccess`, and `NotTeacher` on `/api/admin`.

## Sources

- `.scratch/aula-virtual/program-design/kurasu.md`, branches 3 and 4.
- `.scratch/aula-virtual/tasks.md`, T18; test design rows A71, A74 and A91.
# kurasu: checks and tests

verified: 2026-11-02

Answers which checks reject code in kurasu and where its tests live.

## Knowledge

- oxlint runs type-aware with every rule as an error; oxfmt formats the code.
- A local plugin enforces boundaries: `apps/web` imports only `@kurasu/contract` and `@kurasu/slides` among the project's packages; `packages/core` imports no Cloudflare, Alchemy, Drizzle or jose; `packages/*` never import `apps/*`.
- TypeScript rules: `== null` instead of `=== null` or `=== undefined`; no enums (a const map and a derived type); named exports only.
- The tsconfig compiles with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: an optional prop `?: T` rejects an explicit `undefined`. A prop every caller writes is required and typed `T | undefined`; a prop callers may omit is `?: T | undefined`.
- React rules: arrow-function components with a `Props` interface; React imported by name; conditional rendering with a ternary, never `&&`; no nested ternaries; one component per file; no destructured `useQuery` or `useMutation`.
- The project copies anti-slop into `tools/oxlint/anti-slop/` and adapts it as its own, with its generic and Effect rules.
- `@effect/tsgo` makes `tsc` fail on Effect diagnostics: missing services, `any` in error channels, global `Date`, `fetch` or `console` inside Effect.
- lefthook runs check on every commit; nobody commits with `--no-verify`. The tests run by hand with `pnpm test` before handing work over, because the API suite takes about a minute. turbo caches each package's tests until the package or one of its workspace dependencies changes.
- Tests are integration tests only, in `apps/api/test` (Alchemy's `alchemy/Test/Vitest` in dev mode, HTTP and WebSocket against the local stack) and `apps/web/test` (screens with the real router, the API answered by MSW, Testing Library on happy-dom). Tests live only there: the `test-location` lint rule rejects a test file anywhere else, and the root `projects` list names only the two apps. Before a package whose logic is too complex to cover through the API or the web gets its own tests, extend both the `test-location` rule and the root `projects` list to include it. Tests do not mock modules.
- Two web test helpers control when the mock server answers a request and what it answers. `heldResponse(method, path)` (`test/helpers/held-response.ts`) holds every request to the path until the test calls `release`, so the test can check the screen while the request is still waiting: a skeleton, a pending button. Released without a response, the requests fall through to the handlers already in place. `failingRoute(method, path, status = 500)` (`test/helpers/failing-route.ts`) answers the path with that status and a body no endpoint declares, as a failing server does.
- Pass the handlers that replace the page's own as the `overrides` argument of the test file's `openPage`, which calls `server.use` with them after the page's handlers and before the page renders. If the test calls `server.use` after the page opens, the requests that the page sends while it loads have already reached the page's handlers.
- The web tests wait up to 4 s in Testing Library's `findBy*` and `waitFor` (`configure({ asyncUtilTimeout: 4000 })` in `test/setup.ts`). `/aula` asks for its data in a chain (`/me`, `/sessions`, the session, the materials, the slides). When turbo runs the web and API suites together, the slides iframe appears after about 1.5 s, against about 0.3 s on an idle machine, past the 1 s default.
- To reproduce a web test that fails only under load, run it with about 40 busy-loop processes beside vitest. Running the web suite alone does not reproduce it.
- The five `[MSW] Cannot bypass a request … "error" strategy` messages in a passing web run are expected. They come from tests that navigate away while a request or the classroom socket is in flight.
- Each API test file deploys its own stage: an empty D1 and R2, the migrations, and its fixtures loaded with `importFiles`. The tests in a file share that database, so each test uses its own records. The test stage sets `allowedDestinationAddresses` to the fixtures' emails; a link requested for an email outside the list makes the mail fail. A test reads the mail bodies from the files the local binding writes under `.alchemy/local/email`, and the sender, recipients and subject from the line the binding logs to the stage's Worker log under `.alchemy/log/<stage>/Api` (`test/helpers/sent-mail.ts`); see `alchemy/local-tests`.
- `app/vitest.config.ts` lists the two projects under Vitest 5's `projects` option; there is no `vitest.workspace.ts`. `happy-dom` and `msw` are also installed at the root, so the whole workspace resolves a single copy of vitest.
- The API project runs at most 4 test files at once (`maxWorkers: 4`): more stages starting together overload the local runtime and every file times out. Each run adds about 130 MB to `apps/api/.alchemy` (see `alchemy/local-tests`).
- The 101 MB upload test (A89) is skipped: under a full run the local runtime sometimes drops the connection mid-upload (EPIPE), and in production Cloudflare cuts a body past 100 MB before it reaches the Worker.
- There are no end-to-end tests. Rows marked `test + manual` in the test design are also run by hand with agent-browser against the local stack (`alchemy dev` and Vite).

## Sources

- `.scratch/aula-virtual/program-design/kurasu.md`, branch 9 and Standards.
- `.scratch/aula-virtual/research-tests-alchemy.md`.
- `.scratch/aula-virtual/research-stack-local.md` and `.scratch/aula-virtual/test-design/kurasu.md`.
- `app/lefthook.yml`, `app/turbo.json`, `app/vitest.config.ts`, `app/apps/api/vitest.config.ts`, `app/apps/api/test/materials.test.ts`.
- `.scratch/aula-virtual/implement/report-refactor.md` (T20).
- `app/apps/web/test/helpers/held-response.ts`, `failing-route.ts`, `app/apps/web/test/admin-classroom.test.tsx`.
- `app/apps/web/test/setup.ts`, commit e70c111 (`test(web): wait up to 4 s in findBy and waitFor`).
# Testing against Alchemy's local stack

verified: 2026-11-02

Answers how integration tests run against a local Alchemy 2 stack: how much state a test file gets, how to start from a clean database with fixtures, how to read and fail the mail a Worker sends, and what cannot be made to fail. The facts come from the alchemy source at 2.0.0-beta.83 (commit 9e3c058) and its issues. kurasu's API suite applies them: it deploys one stage per file, loads the fixtures through `importFiles`, reads the mail from `text/*.txt` and the recipients from the stage's Worker log, makes sends fail with `allowedDestinationAddresses`, and sets `sequence.hooks: "list"`.

## Knowledge

- `alchemy/Test/Vitest` with `dev: true` deploys the stack once per `Test.make` call, in `beforeAll`, so once per test file.
- Local data lives in `.alchemy/local/` (`d1/`, `r2/`, `email/`, …) and is shared by every stage. Each local D1 and R2 gets a `dev:<uuid>` id the first time Alchemy reconciles it, stored in the stage's state row. A stage with no state row gets a new id and starts empty.
- There is no API to reset a local D1 or R2 between tests. `destroy` keeps the data, because the local `delete` handlers do nothing. To start clean, deploy a new stage (`Test.make({ stage })` or `deploy(Stack, { stage })`) per test file, or delete `.alchemy/local` and `.alchemy/state` between runs.
- Migrations apply on every deploy. `D1.Database({ importFiles: ["<fixtures>.sql"] })` runs SQL after the migrations, and skips a file whose hash has not changed. The tests of one file share that data, so each test creates or uses its own records.
- The test process has no public client for the local D1. The local D1 and R2 simulators keep their data in SQLite files under `.alchemy/local/d1/cloudflare-runtime-D1DatabaseObject` and `.alchemy/local/r2/cloudflare-runtime-R2BucketObject`, one file per database or bucket named by a hash, plus `metadata.sqlite`. A test opens them read-only with `node:sqlite`, because the stage's Worker keeps them open. The files outlive their stage, so a test finds its stage's database by a value new to the run, such as a record it just created. kurasu reads them through `test/helpers/local-sqlite.ts`, used by `d1.ts` and `r2.ts`.
- The local `send_email` binding writes each message to `.alchemy/local/email/` and logs the path. The builder form (`.send({ from, to, subject, text, html })`) writes `text/<uuid>.txt` and `html/<uuid>.html`, and no `.eml`. Only `sendRaw` with a MIME message writes `<uuid>.eml`. A test reads the files with `fs`. The folder is shared by every file and run, so a test looks for a value unique to that test. The files hold only the bodies. The sender, the recipients (`To`, `Cc`, `Bcc`) and the subject are in the line `send_email binding called with MessageBuilder:` that the binding logs to the Worker's console, which Alchemy writes to `.alchemy/log/<stage>/<worker>/<timestamp>.log` while the test runs; the line also gives the paths of the body files. `allowedDestinationAddresses` checks only `to`, not `bcc`.
- To make a send fail without mocks, declare `allowedDestinationAddresses` (or `allowedSenderAddresses`) on `Cloudflare.Email.SendEmail` for the test stage. A send to an address outside the list throws `email to <addr> not allowed`, which reaches the Worker as `SendEmailError`. The list is fixed at deploy time.
- The harness has no way to make a Durable Object call fail: no fault injection, no eviction and no abort switch.
- Each run of a suite that deploys a stage per file leaves the stages' state, bundles and local data behind. In kurasu's API suite, each run adds about 130 MB to `apps/api/.alchemy`, and nothing removes it.
- Under Vitest's default `sequence.hooks: "stack"`, `afterAll(destroy(Stack))` hangs with `dev: true` (issue #2118). Set `sequence.hooks: "list"`, or use `Test.make({ sidecar: false })`, or drop the `afterAll` destroy.

## Sources

| Asunto | el título de la sesión | `Novedades de la sesión "<título>"` |
| Mensaje | lo que escribe el profe | tal cual; falta si no escribió nada |
| Novedades | cada novedad incluida, de la más vieja a la más nueva | una línea por novedad, con el texto fijo de su tipo, en pasado |
| Link | la sesión | el botón "Ir a la sesión", a la home o a la home con la sesión abierta |

| Tipo de novedad | Nombre | Línea en el mail |
|---|---|---|
| Sesión habilitada | el título de la sesión | `Se habilitó la sesión "<título>".` |
| Material nuevo | el nombre del material | `Se agregó el material "<nombre>".` |
| Encuesta abierta | la consigna de la encuesta | `Se abrió la encuesta "<consigna>".` |
| Preguntas abiertas | el título de la sesión | `Se abrieron las preguntas de la sesión "<título>".` |

El asunto no lleva el número de la sesión, que el estudiante no ve. El cuerpo lleva, en este orden, el mensaje del profe tal como lo escribió, las novedades incluidas y el link a la sesión. Sin mensaje, el cuerpo empieza por las novedades. Sin novedades, lleva el mensaje y el link. Las novedades no llevan link propio: el único link del mail es el de la sesión. Si la sesión es la destacada en el momento del envío, el link lleva a la home, donde la destacada está arriba. Si no, lleva a la home con `?sesion=<id>`, y la home despliega esa sesión en la lista y la deja en el centro de la pantalla (ver [estados de encuestas y sesiones](estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md)). El mail no saluda al estudiante por su nombre y no tiene pie, link para darse de baja ni texto legal.
113:En el inicio, el estudiante ve solo las sesiones habilitadas, en el orden de la lista del profe. Arriba está la sesión destacada, la que tiene la marca. Es la única desde la que se entra al aula. Debajo, "Otras sesiones" lista todas las demás habilitadas en el orden del profe, también las que vienen después de la destacada. Al costado de esa lista, un camino une un círculo por sesión: las sesiones anteriores a la destacada llevan el check de terminada, y las que vienen después no llevan check ni número. Cada card muestra el resumen, las encuestas activas, donde el estudiante vota o deja su feedback, y los links a Material, Encuestas y Preguntas, sin cantidades. Cada link abre un modal, que en celular es una hoja desde abajo y en escritorio va centrado. Cada card que se pliega muestra un caret, que apunta hacia abajo cuando está plegada y hacia arriba cuando está desplegada, como la lista de Presentes. Una sesión de "Otras sesiones" muestra su material, sus encuestas cerradas y sus preguntas para leer, y en ella no se pregunta ni se vota.

docs/architecture/componentes.md:57:Un Worker de assets sirve la web. En el navegador, la web pide todo a la API con la cookie del login y carga las slides de la sesión, un HTML del profe. La web habla con ese HTML por la API de las slides (ver [API de las slides](api-de-las-slides.md)). Mientras el usuario está en el aula, la web mantiene un WebSocket abierto con el aula de la sesión. Lo que no viene del servidor lo guarda en el localStorage del navegador.
docs/architecture/componentes.md:74:El aula de cada sesión es un Durable Object. Mientras el usuario está en el aula, la web tiene un WebSocket abierto con ella. La API le avisa al aula cada cambio que guarda, el aula se lo avisa a las webs conectadas, y cada web le vuelve a pedir a la API lo que cambió. Un deploy reinicia los Durable Objects y corta todas las conexiones del aula. Cómo viaja un cambio y qué pasa cuando se corta la conexión, también en un deploy, está en [tiempo real del aula](tiempo-real-del-aula.md).
docs/architecture/api-de-las-slides.md:79:El profe mueve la slide desde la pestaña Aula del admin de la sesión (1). Su web le dice a su HTML a qué `slide` y `step` ir (2) y le manda la nueva posición a la API (3), que la guarda en D1, en `current_slide` y `current_step` de la sesión (4) y le avisa al aula (5). El aula avisa a los conectados (6), cada web le pide la posición guardada a la API (7, 8), y la de quien sigue al profe lleva su HTML ahí (9) (ver [tiempo real del aula](tiempo-real-del-aula.md)).
docs/architecture/api-de-las-slides.md:87:[Prototipo del aula del estudiante, con la navegación y seguir al profe](../prototipos/aula-responsive.html)
docs/architecture/api-de-las-slides.md:123:En el modal, mientras la web revisa, Subir, el switch y el tacho quedan deshabilitados. Si la revisión falla, el switch vuelve a apagado. El alert verde queda hasta que el profe cierra el modal o apaga el switch. En la lista del material, el alert verde desaparece a los 10 segundos, y el error queda hasta que el profe vuelve a marcar un archivo.
docs/architecture/login-y-acceso.md:94:Antes de pedir el link (2), la web controla el email con la regla de arriba, como controla los campos de cualquier formulario (ver [carga y acciones de la web](carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md)). Si el estudiante aprieta "Mandame el link" con un email inválido, el error de un campo dice "El email ingresado no es válido." y aparece debajo del campo del email. El botón está habilitado mientras haya texto en el campo. Los mensajes de la API, como el de que no está registrado, aparecen como error del formulario antes del botón.

139:La entidad `RaisedHand` une a un estudiante con una sesión. Cada estudiante tiene a lo sumo una por sesión, y la base lo garantiza con un índice único sobre la sesión y el estudiante. Existe hasta que alguien baja la mano, el estudiante o el profe, así que sigue levantada si el estudiante sale del aula y vuelve (ver [tiempo real del aula](tiempo-real-del-aula.md)).
66:Un batch que cruza varios stores lo arma el servicio. Cada puerto que lo necesita ofrece sus escrituras sin ejecutar, y el core las recibe sin ver la sentencia de adentro. Un puerto propio del batch las corre juntas en D1, en el orden en que el servicio las pasa. Así, cambiar la destacada lo arma el servicio de sesiones con escrituras de los stores de sesiones, encuestas y manos levantadas.
82:- **Al instante**: las acciones directas, un botón, un switch o un arrastre, sin confirmación ni formulario. Por ejemplo, deshabilitar una sesión que no es la destacada, dar acceso a un usuario, levantar la mano, marcar una pregunta como respondida, activar o cerrar una encuesta, reordenar las sesiones o mover la slide.
85:Destacar una sesión, sacarle la marca a la destacada, deshabilitar la destacada y habilitar una sesión desde su modal quedan en espera, porque pasan por un diálogo que confirma qué se cierra: si fallan, el error aparece dentro del diálogo, que sigue abierto (ver [estados de encuestas y sesiones](estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md)).
17:- Loading: a part that reads data renders `data == null ? <SkeletonOf>…</SkeletonOf> : …`. `ui/SkeletonOf` wraps the real part filled with example data, kept per topic in `features/<topic>/*-examples.ts`, so the skeleton takes the part's own size. Skeletons are coarse: wrap a whole card (the highlighted session, each card of a folding section, each poll card, each list row, the slide, the header's name and avatar), never the inside of one. `.skeleton` paints the wrapped card as one soft grey block in the theme's colours and hides everything inside it, text, buttons and icons included. It adds the `.skeleton` class, `inert` and `aria-hidden`. It adds `aria-hidden` as well as `inert` because Testing Library ignores `inert`, and a screen reader must not read the example data.
20:- A query that only one role may run waits for the role with `enabled`. The API answers the other role with a 403, `NotStudent` or `NotTeacher`, which is not an access error. When the screen has no data yet, `throwOnError` sends that 403 to the error screen. On `/`, the student's sessions and active polls pass `enabled: me.data?.role === "student"`, so they wait for `me`, and the page draws the student's skeleton meanwhile.

# Consistency check: `feat/preguntas-en-la-card` against `d09d518`

Repository: `/home/agus/.herdr/worktrees/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/feat-preguntas-en-la-card` (kurasu in `app/`). Paths below are relative to that root.

Read: `app/docs/README.md`, every note in `app/docs/architecture/` the change touches, `app/docs/prototipos/README.md` and the prototypes, `app/AGENTS.md`, `.mahou/wiki/` (`INDEX.md`, `web.md`, `fence.md`, `architecture.md`, `api.md`, `alchemy/local-tests.md`), and the code in `packages/core`, `packages/database`, `packages/contract`, `apps/api/src`, `apps/web/src` and the test helpers and fixtures the change touched.

## Leftovers

1. **`app/apps/web/src/features/sessions/rail-look.ts:5`**: `export type RailLook = Exclude<RailNodeLook, "locked" | "new">` is exported, but nothing outside the file imports it (`grep RailLook` finds only `rail-look.ts:5` and `:10`). `RailNodeLook` in `RailNode.tsx` is the type that lists the looks, and `SessionRailNode` takes `Exclude<RailNodeLook, "new">`. Fix: drop the `export`, or inline the return type of `railLook`.

2. **`app/packages/database/src/database.ts:9`**: `export interface Statement { toSQL: … }` is the same structural type as the core's `Write` (`packages/core/src/batch.ts:6`). Since the change, `repositoryOf` builds `Write`s and `D1Batch` passes `Write`s to `batch(client, …)`, which is still typed `ReadonlyArray<Statement>`; `repository.ts:41` and `:64` still import and use `Statement`. Two names exist for one shape. Fix: type `batch` and the repository's `Write<R>` with the core's `Write` and delete `Statement`.

## Docs vs code

1. **The featured switch fails silently when no other session is featured.** `app/apps/web/src/features/sessions/FeaturedSwitch.tsx:56-59` featuring a session when `featured == null` calls `update.mutate({ … featured: true })` with no dialog, and `useUpdateSession.ts:32-40` (`toastOf`) returns `undefined` for `{ featured: true }`, so a failed request shows nothing. Docs: `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md:85` says "Destacar una sesión … queda[n] en espera, porque pasan por un diálogo … si fallan, el error aparece dentro del diálogo", and `invariantes.md` says "Una acción en espera muestra su error dentro de su formulario o modal". The code has no dialog in this case and no toast either. Fix: give `{ featured: true }` a toast in `toastOf` (the "toast cuando no tiene ninguno de los dos" path of `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md`), and change line 85 to say the dialog appears only when another session is featured. The alternative is to always confirm featuring.

2. **Disabling the featured session shows its error twice.** `EnabledSwitch.tsx:47-58` runs `update.mutateAsync({ change: { enabled: false } })` inside `ConfirmAction`, so the dialog shows `updateErrorText`. `toastOf` (`useUpdateSession.ts:38-40`) also returns "No se pudo deshabilitar la sesión." for any `enabled: false` without `featured`, and it does not check whether the session is the featured one, so a toast appears as well. `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md:85` and `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` ("si fallan, el error aparece dentro del diálogo, que sigue abierto") describe only the in-dialog error. Fix: let the caller turn off the toast for the confirmed path, for example by passing the session's `featured` in `SessionUpdate`, or by moving the toast to the instant caller's `onError`.

3. **`app/docs/architecture/acceso-a-datos.md:76-77`** ("Por qué una sentencia de batch no devuelve filas") says "una sentencia de batch no devuelve nada". In code, `repository.ts:227-229` builds `writes.update` and `writes.updateWhere` with `.returning({ id: table.id })`, and `removing` (`repository.ts:206-211`, used by `writes.remove` and `writes.removeWhere`) uses `.returning()` with every column. These writes now go into `Batch.run` in `Sessions.updateLeaving` (`hands.writes.removeWhere`, `store.writes.update`, `polls.writes.updateWhere`), in addition to the existing material batches. The batch drops the rows (`database.ts:52`, `Effect.asVoid`), so what is true is that *the batch* returns nothing, not that the statement does. This predates the change, but the change makes the core depend on it. Fix: reword the callout to say that `Batch.run` (and `repository.batch`) returns nothing and discards what the statements return.

4. **`app/docs/architecture/modelo-de-datos.md:139`** says "[La mano] Existe hasta que alguien baja la mano, el estudiante o el profe". `Sessions.updateLeaving` (`packages/core/src/sessions/sessions.ts:139`) also removes every hand of a session that stops being featured, as `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` and `acceso-a-datos.md` say. Fix: add "o hasta que la sesión deja de ser la destacada (ver [estados de encuestas y sesiones](estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md))". `tiempo-real-del-aula.md:68` ("La mano sigue levantada si el estudiante sale y vuelve, hasta que alguien la baja.") needs the same clause.

5. **Prototypes that still number the sessions.** `app/docs/prototipos/piezas.html:219` draws each rail node with `${i + 1}` and the `live` look for every enabled session. `app/docs/prototipos/marca-cuervo.html:201,211,218` draws a numbered node and the kicker "Sesión 2 de ${SESSIONS.length}". The code draws no number and no "Sesión N de M" (`SessionRailNode.tsx`, `AdminFeatured.tsx`, `FeaturedSession.tsx`), and `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` states "Ningún círculo lleva número". These prototypes are linked from `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md` and `componentes.md` for other subjects (the shared pieces, the brand), so the session list in them is background. Fix: draw the nodes with the check, star or empty looks and drop the kicker, or add a line to `prototipos/README.md` saying that their session list is not the current one.

## Code vs code

1. **`app/apps/web/test/helpers/session-store.ts:50-58`** mimics the API when a session is featured or disabled: it sets `featured: false` on the session that leaves. It leaves `featuredQuestions` as it was. The API (`Sessions.updateLeaving`, `sessions.ts:134`) writes `{ featured: false, featuredQuestions: false }` to the leaving session. A test that disables, unmarks or replaces a featured session with featured questions on then sees `featuredQuestions: true` on a session that is not featured, a state the API never returns (`modelo-de-datos.md`: "solo la destacada tiene `featured_questions` en verdadero"). Fix: set `featuredQuestions: false` wherever the helper sets `featured: false`.

## Vocabulary

1. **`app/packages/database/src/repository.ts:225` and `:275`**: the comment "A statement reads nothing after its write, so several can go in one D1 batch." sits above `const writes`, and `batch: (statements: ReadonlyArray<Statement>) => …` keeps the old name for its parameter, although the change renamed `statements` to `writes`. Fix: "A write reads nothing after itself…" and `batch: (writes: ReadonlyArray<Write>) => …` (see Leftovers 2).

2. **`app/packages/core/src/hands/hands.ts:15-17`**: "A student raises and lowers their own in an enabled session". `raise` and `lowerOwn` now require `featuredSession` (`hands.ts:62,74`). Fix: "in the featured session".

3. **`app/packages/core/src/questions/questions.ts:82`**: "An open question of an enabled session: what the student can act on." `findOpenQuestion` now checks `featuredSession` (`:91`). Fix: "of the featured session". The service comment at `:35-38` ("The student sees the open questions of enabled sessions … votes at most once each … and deletes only their own") puts reading and writing in one sentence. Reading is still any enabled session, but asking, voting and deleting are now limited to the featured one. Fix: add "and asks, votes and deletes only in the featured session".

4. **`.mahou/wiki/web.md:17`**: "wrap a whole card (the highlighted session, each card of a folding section, …)". The code calls this card the featured session (`FeaturedSession`, `AdminFeatured`), and `HighlightedSession` no longer exists. Fix: "the featured session". The line is not false about skeletons, so the entry needs no other change.

5. **`app/apps/web/test/loading.test.tsx:67-79`**: the variables `highlighted`, `earlier` and `earlierCards` name the featured card and the "Todas las sesiones" section, which the change renamed from the highlighted session and `EarlierSessions`. Fix: `featuredCard`, `allSessions`, `allCards`.

6. **`app/docs/prototipos/inicio-responsive.html:100,297-309,336,452,472,478,508,594,616,712`**: the prototype's state key and helper are `highlighted` / `highlightedIn`, and its comments say "highlighted card" and "highlighted session". `:508` says "Only the highlighted session takes new questions and votes; earlier ones are read-only", but every non-featured session is read-only, including the ones after it (`estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md`: "Cualquier otra sesión de la lista … en ella no se pregunta ni se vota"; `SessionLinks` passes `readOnly={!featured}`). Fix: rename to `featured` / `featuredIn`, and change `:508` to "every other session is read-only".

## Not reported

- `app/apps/web/src/routes/_app/index.tsx:46-47`: the empty-state text "Cuando el profe habilite la primera, aparece acá arriba." could look like a leftover of the "last enabled" rule. The prototype (`inicio-responsive.html:487`) keeps the same text, and the enable modal features the session by default, so this follows a recorded design.
- `app/apps/web/test/fixtures/content.ts:22` `lastFeatured(...)`: it marks the last session of a fixture list as featured, explicitly. It builds data for the new rule and does not rely on the old derived one.
- `app/apps/api/test/unfeatured.test.ts:21,41`: the test names mention "the last enabled one" to check that the old rule no longer applies.
- `app/packages/core/src/announcements/announcements.ts:49`: `const visibleSessions = yield* Sessions` is used only for `featured()`. The name comes from commit `1b2a4e3`, before `d09d518`, and does not describe a student write.
- `app/docs/prototipos/aula-responsive.html:196`: "Sesión 2 de 6" is the text of an example slide, not app UI.
- Remaining `visibleSession` calls (`hands.ts:51`, `questions.ts:100`, `polls.ts:171`, `materials.ts:69`, `sessions.ts:164`) are student reads, which `invariantes.md` allows on any enabled session.
- `.mahou/wiki/architecture.md`, `api.md`, `fence.md`, `alchemy/local-tests.md` and `app/AGENTS.md`: no line is made false by the change. They do not mention `NotFeatured`, `SwitchButton`, `count-label`, `findFeatured`, `switch-row`, `blush`/`wine` or the third type parameter of `useApiQuery`. That information is missing, but nothing there contradicts the code.

# Consistency check: `feat/preguntas-en-la-card` against `d09d518`

Repository: `/home/agus/.herdr/worktrees/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/feat-preguntas-en-la-card` (kurasu in `app/`). Paths below are relative to that root.

Read: `app/docs/README.md`, every note in `app/docs/architecture/` the change touches, `app/docs/prototipos/README.md` and the prototypes, `app/AGENTS.md`, `.mahou/wiki/` (`INDEX.md`, `web.md`, `fence.md`, `architecture.md`, `api.md`, `alchemy/local-tests.md`), and the code in `packages/core`, `packages/database`, `packages/contract`, `apps/api/src`, `apps/web/src` and the test helpers and fixtures the change touched.

## Leftovers

1. **`app/apps/web/src/features/sessions/rail-look.ts:5`**: `export type RailLook = Exclude<RailNodeLook, "locked" | "new">` is exported, but nothing outside the file imports it (`grep RailLook` finds only `rail-look.ts:5` and `:10`). `RailNodeLook` in `RailNode.tsx` is the type that lists the looks, and `SessionRailNode` takes `Exclude<RailNodeLook, "new">`. Fix: drop the `export`, or inline the return type of `railLook`.

2. **`app/packages/database/src/database.ts:9`**: `export interface Statement { toSQL: … }` is the same structural type as the core's `Write` (`packages/core/src/batch.ts:6`). Since the change, `repositoryOf` builds `Write`s and `D1Batch` passes `Write`s to `batch(client, …)`, which is still typed `ReadonlyArray<Statement>`; `repository.ts:41` and `:64` still import and use `Statement`. Two names exist for one shape. Fix: type `batch` and the repository's `Write<R>` with the core's `Write` and delete `Statement`.

## Docs vs code

1. **The featured switch fails silently when no other session is featured.** `app/apps/web/src/features/sessions/FeaturedSwitch.tsx:56-59` featuring a session when `featured == null` calls `update.mutate({ … featured: true })` with no dialog, and `useUpdateSession.ts:32-40` (`toastOf`) returns `undefined` for `{ featured: true }`, so a failed request shows nothing. Docs: `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md:85` says "Destacar una sesión … queda[n] en espera, porque pasan por un diálogo … si fallan, el error aparece dentro del diálogo", and `invariantes.md` says "Una acción en espera muestra su error dentro de su formulario o modal". The code has no dialog in this case and no toast either. Fix: give `{ featured: true }` a toast in `toastOf` (the "toast cuando no tiene ninguno de los dos" path of `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md`), and change line 85 to say the dialog appears only when another session is featured. The alternative is to always confirm featuring.

2. **Disabling the featured session shows its error twice.** `EnabledSwitch.tsx:47-58` runs `update.mutateAsync({ change: { enabled: false } })` inside `ConfirmAction`, so the dialog shows `updateErrorText`. `toastOf` (`useUpdateSession.ts:38-40`) also returns "No se pudo deshabilitar la sesión." for any `enabled: false` without `featured`, and it does not check whether the session is the featured one, so a toast appears as well. `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md:85` and `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` ("si fallan, el error aparece dentro del diálogo, que sigue abierto") describe only the in-dialog error. Fix: let the caller turn off the toast for the confirmed path, for example by passing the session's `featured` in `SessionUpdate`, or by moving the toast to the instant caller's `onError`.

3. **`app/docs/architecture/acceso-a-datos.md:76-77`** ("Por qué una sentencia de batch no devuelve filas") says "una sentencia de batch no devuelve nada". In code, `repository.ts:227-229` builds `writes.update` and `writes.updateWhere` with `.returning({ id: table.id })`, and `removing` (`repository.ts:206-211`, used by `writes.remove` and `writes.removeWhere`) uses `.returning()` with every column. These writes now go into `Batch.run` in `Sessions.updateLeaving` (`hands.writes.removeWhere`, `store.writes.update`, `polls.writes.updateWhere`), in addition to the existing material batches. The batch drops the rows (`database.ts:52`, `Effect.asVoid`), so what is true is that *the batch* returns nothing, not that the statement does. This predates the change, but the change makes the core depend on it. Fix: reword the callout to say that `Batch.run` (and `repository.batch`) returns nothing and discards what the statements return.

4. **`app/docs/architecture/modelo-de-datos.md:139`** says "[La mano] Existe hasta que alguien baja la mano, el estudiante o el profe". `Sessions.updateLeaving` (`packages/core/src/sessions/sessions.ts:139`) also removes every hand of a session that stops being featured, as `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` and `acceso-a-datos.md` say. Fix: add "o hasta que la sesión deja de ser la destacada (ver [estados de encuestas y sesiones](estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md))". `tiempo-real-del-aula.md:68` ("La mano sigue levantada si el estudiante sale y vuelve, hasta que alguien la baja.") needs the same clause.

5. **Prototypes that still number the sessions.** `app/docs/prototipos/piezas.html:219` draws each rail node with `${i + 1}` and the `live` look for every enabled session. `app/docs/prototipos/marca-cuervo.html:201,211,218` draws a numbered node and the kicker "Sesión 2 de ${SESSIONS.length}". The code draws no number and no "Sesión N de M" (`SessionRailNode.tsx`, `AdminFeatured.tsx`, `FeaturedSession.tsx`), and `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` states "Ningún círculo lleva número". These prototypes are linked from `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md` and `componentes.md` for other subjects (the shared pieces, the brand), so the session list in them is background. Fix: draw the nodes with the check, star or empty looks and drop the kicker, or add a line to `prototipos/README.md` saying that their session list is not the current one.

## Code vs code

1. **`app/apps/web/test/helpers/session-store.ts:50-58`** mimics the API when a session is featured or disabled: it sets `featured: false` on the session that leaves. It leaves `featuredQuestions` as it was. The API (`Sessions.updateLeaving`, `sessions.ts:134`) writes `{ featured: false, featuredQuestions: false }` to the leaving session. A test that disables, unmarks or replaces a featured session with featured questions on then sees `featuredQuestions: true` on a session that is not featured, a state the API never returns (`modelo-de-datos.md`: "solo la destacada tiene `featured_questions` en verdadero"). Fix: set `featuredQuestions: false` wherever the helper sets `featured: false`.

## Vocabulary

1. **`app/packages/database/src/repository.ts:225` and `:275`**: the comment "A statement reads nothing after its write, so several can go in one D1 batch." sits above `const writes`, and `batch: (statements: ReadonlyArray<Statement>) => …` keeps the old name for its parameter, although the change renamed `statements` to `writes`. Fix: "A write reads nothing after itself…" and `batch: (writes: ReadonlyArray<Write>) => …` (see Leftovers 2).

2. **`app/packages/core/src/hands/hands.ts:15-17`**: "A student raises and lowers their own in an enabled session". `raise` and `lowerOwn` now require `featuredSession` (`hands.ts:62,74`). Fix: "in the featured session".

3. **`app/packages/core/src/questions/questions.ts:82`**: "An open question of an enabled session: what the student can act on." `findOpenQuestion` now checks `featuredSession` (`:91`). Fix: "of the featured session". The service comment at `:35-38` ("The student sees the open questions of enabled sessions … votes at most once each … and deletes only their own") puts reading and writing in one sentence. Reading is still any enabled session, but asking, voting and deleting are now limited to the featured one. Fix: add "and asks, votes and deletes only in the featured session".

4. **`.mahou/wiki/web.md:17`**: "wrap a whole card (the highlighted session, each card of a folding section, …)". The code calls this card the featured session (`FeaturedSession`, `AdminFeatured`), and `HighlightedSession` no longer exists. Fix: "the featured session". The line is not false about skeletons, so the entry needs no other change.

5. **`app/apps/web/test/loading.test.tsx:67-79`**: the variables `highlighted`, `earlier` and `earlierCards` name the featured card and the "Todas las sesiones" section, which the change renamed from the highlighted session and `EarlierSessions`. Fix: `featuredCard`, `allSessions`, `allCards`.

6. **`app/docs/prototipos/inicio-responsive.html:100,297-309,336,452,472,478,508,594,616,712`**: the prototype's state key and helper are `highlighted` / `highlightedIn`, and its comments say "highlighted card" and "highlighted session". `:508` says "Only the highlighted session takes new questions and votes; earlier ones are read-only", but every non-featured session is read-only, including the ones after it (`estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md`: "Cualquier otra sesión de la lista … en ella no se pregunta ni se vota"; `SessionLinks` passes `readOnly={!featured}`). Fix: rename to `featured` / `featuredIn`, and change `:508` to "every other session is read-only".

## Not reported

- `app/apps/web/src/routes/_app/index.tsx:46-47`: the empty-state text "Cuando el profe habilite la primera, aparece acá arriba." could look like a leftover of the "last enabled" rule. The prototype (`inicio-responsive.html:487`) keeps the same text, and the enable modal features the session by default, so this follows a recorded design.
- `app/apps/web/test/fixtures/content.ts:22` `lastFeatured(...)`: it marks the last session of a fixture list as featured, explicitly. It builds data for the new rule and does not rely on the old derived one.
- `app/apps/api/test/unfeatured.test.ts:21,41`: the test names mention "the last enabled one" to check that the old rule no longer applies.
- `app/packages/core/src/announcements/announcements.ts:49`: `const visibleSessions = yield* Sessions` is used only for `featured()`. The name comes from commit `1b2a4e3`, before `d09d518`, and does not describe a student write.
- `app/docs/prototipos/aula-responsive.html:196`: "Sesión 2 de 6" is the text of an example slide, not app UI.
- Remaining `visibleSession` calls (`hands.ts:51`, `questions.ts:100`, `polls.ts:171`, `materials.ts:69`, `sessions.ts:164`) are student reads, which `invariantes.md` allows on any enabled session.
- `.mahou/wiki/architecture.md`, `api.md`, `fence.md`, `alchemy/local-tests.md` and `app/AGENTS.md`: no line is made false by the change. They do not mention `NotFeatured`, `SwitchButton`, `count-label`, `findFeatured`, `switch-row`, `blush`/`wine` or the third type parameter of `useApiQuery`. That information is missing, but nothing there contradicts the code.
